get.description: upgrades the connection to a websocket. the client sends requests as {"id", "subject", "payload"} and receives replies as {"request_id", "payload"}; the subject must be one the server consumes.

approved.description:
Approved is the answer. A request that is not approved is refused, and
the application is told so at the address it registered.

request.description:
RequestToken is the authorization request as the authorization endpoint
signed it.

aliases.description:
Aliases are the names its neighbours on that network reach it by, beside
its own.

network.description: Network is the network's id or its name.

protocol.description: Protocol is tcp or udp; empty is tcp.

cpus.description: CPUs is in cores and Memory in bytes; zero is no limit beyond the VM's.

env.description: Env is the environment, each as KEY=value.

image.description: Image is pulled first when the VM does not hold it.

name.description: Name is docker's name for it; empty lets docker pick one.

networks.description:
Networks are the VM's docker networks to attach it to, beside the
default one.

ports.description:
Ports publish container ports on the VM. A VM port the VM also exposes
through the ingress is reachable from outside; any other is reachable
only from inside the VM.

restart_policy.description: RestartPolicy is no, always, unless-stopped or on-failure.

vm.description:
VM is the Docker VM the container went into, and whether it was made
for it.

driver.description:
Driver is bridge, which is also what empty is: a VM is a single docker
host, and no other driver has anything to join there.

internal.description: Internal keeps the containers on it from reaching anything outside it.

compose.description:
Compose is the YAML, as it would be handed to docker compose. What it
calls its project is ignored: the stack's slug is the project.

vm.description:
VM is the Docker VM the stack went into, and whether it was made for
it.

image.description:
Image is the OCI reference a machine boots from; empty takes its
kind's default, and a Docker VM is always the workload's own image.

kind.description:
Kind is machine, an OS image somebody opens a terminal in, or docker,
the image containers and stacks are run in.

lifetime_seconds.description:
LifetimeSeconds is how long the VM is kept before it is deleted, and
zero keeps it until somebody deletes it.

persistent_disk.description:
PersistentDisk keeps what is written to the disk across a stop and a
start; without it the disk is as the image left it on every start.

ports.description: Ports are the guest ports the ingress serves, while ingress allows it.

snapshot_uuid.description:
SnapshotUUID makes the VM from one of the caller's snapshots: its kind
and image are the snapshot's, and its disk the larger of the one asked
for and the snapshot's.

driver.description:
Driver is local, which is also what empty is: a volume lives on the
VM's own disk.

truncated.description:
Truncated says there was more than one answer carries: what is here is
the last of it.

disk.description: Disk is the disk, in bytes, a VM it is restored onto needs at least.

engine.description: Engine is what took it; only the same engine can restore it.

size.description: Size is how many bytes it takes where it is kept.

vm_uuid.description: VMUUID and VMName are the VM it was taken of, which may be gone since.

compose.description:
Compose is the YAML as it was given. A listing leaves it out: it is
as long as somebody wrote it, and a listing is read to choose one.

note.description:
Note says why there are no containers when it is not that the stack has
none: NoteVMNotRunning.

output.description: Output is the tail of what the last compose command printed.

slug.description:
Slug is the compose project's name inside the VM, which its containers
carry as their stack.

state.description:
State is what the last compose command left it as; ExpectedState is
what it was asked to be, running or stopped.

vm_uuid.description: VMUUID is the Docker VM it is deployed into.

lifetime_seconds.description:
LifetimeSeconds is how long the VM is kept, and zero is until it is
deleted. ExpiresAt is when one with a lifetime goes.

ports.description: Ports are the guest ports the ingress serves, sorted.

reason.description: Reason is why it failed, or what is pending, when the workload can say.

slug.description: Slug is the name its ports are served under.

state.description:
State is what the VM is doing; ExpectedState is what it was asked to be
doing. They differ while the workload is closing the gap.

stats.description:
Stats is the last sample its node reported, and is left out until there
is one.

urls.description: URLs are where its ports are served, while its ingress allows it.

truncated.description:
Truncated says there was more than one answer carries: what is here is
the last of it.

impersonated_by.description:
ImpersonatedBy is who is seeing the dashboard as this user. It is absent
from an ordinary session, and is what lets the dashboard say whose eyes
these are without being told by whoever is holding the token.

user.description:
User is who the tokens are for. The caller has just been handed a session
that is not theirs, so it is told whose it is, and does not have to ask.

read.description:
Read carries the toggle's new state: true stamps the read time, false
clears it back to unread.

stack.description:
Stack and Service are the compose project and service it belongs to,
when a stack deployed it. The project is the stack's slug, and
StackUUID is the stack's uuid when the request could see that stack.

state.description:
State is docker's: created, running, paused, restarting, removing,
exited or dead. Status is the sentence docker puts it in.

containers.description: Containers are the containers attached to it.

in_use.description: InUse says a container was created from it.

disk.description: Disk is the disk, in bytes, a VM it is restored onto needs at least.

engine.description: Engine is what took it; only the same engine can restore it.

size.description: Size is how many bytes it takes where it is kept.

vm_uuid.description: VMUUID and VMName are the VM it was taken of, which may be gone since.

Compose is the YAML as it was given. A listing leaves it out: it is

LifetimeSeconds is how long the VM is kept, and zero is until it is

ports.description: Ports are the guest ports the ingress serves, sorted.

reason.description: Reason is why it failed, or what is pending, when the workload can say.

slug.description: Slug is the name its ports are served under.

state.description:
State is what the VM is doing; ExpectedState is what it was asked to be

stats.description:

urls.description: URLs are where its ports are served, while its ingress allows it.

stack.description:
Stack and Service are the compose project and service it belongs to,
when a stack deployed it. The project is the stack's slug, and
StackUUID is the stack's uuid when the request could see that stack.

state.description:
State is docker's: created, running, paused, restarting, removing,
exited or dead. Status is the sentence docker puts it in.

in_use.description: InUse says a container mounts it.

reference.description: Reference is the image, as name[:tag] or name@digest.

client_secret.description:
ClientSecret is handed over once, here, and is never readable again. It
is absent for a public client, which has none.

client_secret_expires_at.description:
ClientSecretExpiresAt is zero for a secret that does not expire, and
[RFC 7591] asks for it whenever a secret was issued, zero included.

[RFC 7591]: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591

snapshot_uuid.description:
SnapshotUUID is the snapshot whose disk replaces the VM's: one of its
owner's, of the same kind and engine, and no larger than its disk.

lifetime_seconds.description:
LifetimeSeconds counts again from now, and zero keeps the VM until it
is deleted.

ports.description: Ports replace the ones it has; an empty list exposes none.
